summary: Charlotte Melina Viall studied at the University of Chicago from around 1910 to 1914 and at the Cornell University College of Agriculture and Life Sciences.

Charlotte Vaudeville was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at the Sorbonne and École des chartes, studying under Pierre Meile, Louis Renou, Theodor Bloch, and Dhirendra Varma. She held posts at CNRS, EFEO, EPHE, and the Sorbonne.

Chatral Sangye Dorje was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who succeeded Dudjom Rinpoche. He studied under numerous teachers, including Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Sera Khandro, and taught figures such as Keith Dowman and Gyurme Dorje.

Chatsumarn Kabilsingh worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, earning degrees from Visva-Bharati, McMaster, and Magadh universities. She served in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at Thammasat University from circa 1973 to 2000.

Chen-kuo Lin is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his degree at Temple University. He served as Professor and Distinguished Professor at National Chengchi University and held posts at IIAS and Leiden University.
Cheng Huang has held academic posts at the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, UT Southwestern Medical Center, and Southern Methodist University.
Cheng Yen is a religious studies and Buddhist studies figure who studied as a disciple under Yinshun in 1963. She founded the Tzu Chi Foundation in 1966 and Tzu Chi University in 2000.
Cheryl A. Crowley is a Japanology scholar who studied under Linda H. Chance, William R. LaFleur, Philip Boas Yampolsky, and Ryuichi Abe.

Chhabilal Neupane is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed a Master of Arts in Hindi at Indira Gandhi National Open University. He taught at Union Academy Senior Secondary School and held a Darshan post at Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University.

Chheangkhy Hok is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who has held posts at the University of Heng Samrin Thbongkhmum in the Department of Khmer Literature and at the Indian Institute of Technology (BHU) Varanasi.
Chhime Rigdzing was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and held a post at Visva-Bharati University.

Chhimed Rigdzin worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies and studied under Choying Khyabdel. He held a research post at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East and was Professor of Tibetan at Visva-Bharati University from circa 1957 to 1987.
Chi Chen Ho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD from UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., studied under Hsuan Hua, and served as a Teaching Assistant at UCLA.
Chi-chiang Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history, earning a PhD from the University of Arizona in 1986 under Jing-shen Tao and studying under Robert M. Gimello.

Chi-wah Chan is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who earned a PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Benjamin A. Elman. He served as a Teaching Assistant at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Chia Theng Shen was active in Buddhist studies, serving at the Buddhist Association of the United States from circa 1964 to 2007 and founding the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions.
Chie Ikeya is a historian who completed a PhD at Cornell University in 2006, where she studied under David K. Wyatt.
Chien Y. Hsu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under doctoral supervisors Leslie S. Kawamura and James B. Apple, as well as traditional teacher Zhenhua.
Chien-hsing Ho is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology who held posts at Nanhua University as Associate Professor of Religious Studies and at Academia Sinica.

Chienlin Lee earned a PhD at National Dong Hwa University. Lee held posts as an Adjunct Assistant Professor at National Taitung University, Project Assistant Professor at National Dong Hwa University, and Postdoctoral Fellow at Academia Sinica.
